findings.evidence: The file's own docstring at lines 87-90 gives exactly this argument to justify not tagging `nonempty_linearEquiv_spechtModule_asModule_iff`: "`(spechtModule μ).ρ` is not a simp normal form, because the `simp` lemma `FDRep.of_ρ'` unfolds it to the composite". The same term occurs on the RHS tagged here.
findings.fix: Remove `@[simp]` from `spechtModuleClass_def`; keep it as the named defining equation for `rw`, as its two in-file users already do (lines 102, 138). This is how `simpleModuleClass` is handled in RingTheory/Semisimple/RegularIsotypicComponent.lean:206, which has no simp def-equation. Keep `@[simp]` on `partitionEquivSimpleModuleClasses_apply`, whose RHS is then normal.
findings.issue: `@[simp] spechtModuleClass_def` fires wrongly. Its RHS is not a simp normal form: `spechtModule μ` is `FDRep.of (…)` (Specht/Module.lean:314-317) and `FDRep.of_ρ'` is `@[simp]` in Mathlib (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/FDRep.lean:127-129), so simp continues to `simpleModuleClass _ (Representation.asModule (MonoidHom.comp (spechtSubrepresentation (diagramOf μ)).toRepresentation ↑(finCongr _).permCongrHom))`. Since `partitionEquivSimpleModuleClasses_apply` (line 126) is also `@[simp]`, that composite becomes the simp normal form of both `spechtModuleClass μ` and `partitionEquivSimpleModuleClasses n μ`, undoing the point of making `spechtModuleClass` an unexposed `def`.

findings.evidence: Lines 72-83 prove `equivOfAsModuleLinearEquiv (asModuleLinearEquivOfEquiv φ) = φ` and its converse — the two `Equiv` fields. Mathlib states the map-level dictionary in bundled form, `Representation.IntertwiningMap.equivLinearMapAsModule` (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Intertwining.lean:491), so the isomorphism-level one should be bundled too.
findings.fix: Add `noncomputable def Representation.equivEquivAsModuleLinearEquiv : ρ.Equiv σ ≃ (ρ.asModule ≃ₗ[k[G]] σ.asModule)` built from the two functions and the two round-trip lemmas, and derive `nonempty_equiv_iff` as `Equiv.nonempty_congr _`.
findings.issue: The dictionary is incomplete as an interface: `equivOfAsModuleLinearEquiv` and `asModuleLinearEquivOfEquiv` are proved mutually inverse (lines 72-83), i.e. the file has all the data of a bijection, but only `Nonempty (ρ.Equiv σ) ↔ Nonempty (ρ.asModule ≃ₗ[k[G]] σ.asModule)` is exposed. A consumer that needs to transport along the correspondence (counting isomorphism classes, or moving a family of isomorphisms) must rebuild the `Equiv` itself.

findings.evidence: Independence.lean:204-211 `theorem card_le_card_conjClasses … : Fintype.card ι ≤ Nat.card (ConjClasses G)` under the section variables at Independence.lean (`[IsAlgClosed k] [Invertible (Nat.card G : k)]`); semisimplicity of `k[G]` follows from `Invertible (Nat.card G : k)` by Maschke, as already done at CharacterTable/Completeness.lean:260.
findings.fix: Re-derive Independence.lean:204 from `card_simpleSubmoduleClasses_le_card_conjClasses` — send `i ↦ simpleModuleClass k[G] (ρ i).asModule`, injective by `simpleModuleClass_eq_iff` together with the new `Representation.nonempty_equiv_iff` — and drop `[IsAlgClosed k]` there, leaving one canonical bound. `card_le_card_conjClasses_fdRep` (Independence.lean:213) can stay as it is, since `CategoryTheory.Simple` has no dictionary to `Representation.IsIrreducible` (noted at CharacterTable/Completeness.lean:55).
findings.issue: Duplicated public API for the same bound. `TauCeti.ClassFunction.card_le_card_conjClasses` (RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/Independence.lean:204) already states that pairwise inequivalent irreducibles are at most the conjugacy classes, but under `[IsAlgClosed k] [Invertible (Nat.card G : k)]`. The new theorem proves the same bound with no splitting hypothesis, and neither statement mentions the other, so the post-PR surface offers two bounds of which the older carries a hypothesis that is now known to be superfluous.

summary: The `@[simp]` on `spechtModuleClass_def` destroys the abstraction it was introduced to protect: simp unfolds it and then rewrites `(spechtModule μ).ρ` into the `spechtSubrepresentation` composite, by the author's own normal-form argument used elsewhere in the same file. Two smaller interface gaps: the AsModule dictionary proves both round trips but never bundles them as an `Equiv`, and the new counting bound duplicates an existing public bound that keeps a now-unnecessary `IsAlgClosed` hypothesis.
